main_text.l: cia in ius vocabantur, & ebrietatem excusa-
bant, excusationem non recipiebat: sed du-
plici poena eos dignos iudicabat, tum quod
ebrietatem intemperatia sibi contraxissent,
tum quod per ebrietatem deliquissent. Hæc
sententia in Olynthiacis à Demosthene est
illustrata similitudine rerum domesticarum
& humanorum corporum, in quibus parua
incommoda initio accepta & neglecta, ma-
ximam postea calamitatem afferunt. In æ-
dificijs parua domus vitia neglecta magnam
sæpe ruinam trahunt, in corporibus exi-
guæ morborum offensiones aut occultæ
aut neglectæ, maxima vi tandem erumpunt,
ipsumque hominem opprimunt. Idem ac-
cidit in re familiari, in qua parua damna de-
trimentaq; in principio neglecta difsipatio-
nem patrimonij attulerunt.
Tertiò ab immoderato usu vini abstinen-
dum, quia vinum apostatare facit, siue de-
prauat sapientes, [illegible, ~8 letters] / [illegible, ~8 letters]
oder [illegible, ~7 letters] / & arguit, id est, arguendos facit
sensatos. Aufert enim cor, ut Hoseas 4. ait
cap. & grauat cor (quod sedes sapientiæ di-
citur) quemadmodum Christus Iesus testa-
tur, Luc. 21. Proinde gentiles, ut turpitudi-
nem ebrietatis quodammodo demonstra-
rent, Bacchum, ab incondita ebriorum voce
isto nomine denotarunt. Fingunt enim nu-
dum, propter impudentiam: nam ebriosos
deserit pudor: vel propter paupertatem, quod
ebrietatis studiosi ad inopiam redigantur.

page.notes: The Greek and Hebrew words after "sapientes," and the German word in black letter are too damaged to read reliably and are marked illegible. The Hebrew word before "& arguit" is also unreadable. The number "213" and the running head are uncertain; the first letter of the running head is a decorated capital. Long s has been written as plain s throughout, so "Hofeas" appears as "Hoseas" and "fensatos" as "sensatos". Hyphens at line ends are kept as printed.
